title: Younger players he likes and hearing Dexter Gordon at the Vanguard
summary: He praises John Hicks, Walter Booker and Ricky Ford, and recalls an evening with Dexter Gordon at the Vanguard and hearing Slide Hampton.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: To return to more recent months here, I was curious to know--both from your being back here on these three occasions and I know you also keep up with the music down there in Charlottesville--what are some of the younger players that have impressed you most, either saxophone players or whoever?

Well John Hicks and Walter Booker, because they have the right mental attitude. And I heard this little young tenor player, Ricky Ford; he has the right mental attitude. And, well you know that I was so busy since I been here that I haven't had really a chance to get around to hear, you know, a lot of the people that I would like to hear, but those three people, yeah, you know the younger people.
You have had a chance on a couple of occasions to visit around in places, I guess back in the end of December ('79) when you came in and
visited the Vanguard. You might say a little bit about that.

Well, you know, you told me that Dexter was in town, so I knew Dexter since 1941 when he was with Lionel Hampton and then his father was Duke Ellington's doctor. His father was a doctor. And so, you know, I knew Dexter through the years and we did a concert in Groningen, Holland, in '76, I think it was and we spoke briefly. But when I came back to New York and he was at the Village Vanguard, you told me he'd be there, and we had the night off before I went to work. And it was just a wonderful evening. Dexter was playing his heart out and he was such a nice person and we went all the way back and we just had a good time all night. I really enjoyed that. And Dexter is really blowin', he's really playin' and he's got the right attitude about everything. And I thoroughly enjoyed that evening. And then I went by and heard Slide Hampton, one night, I think it was the night before or it was that same night. Anyway, he sounded really good.
What was that, at the Sweet Basil? I saw him; he sounded good.
